note: The operator asked for a doc noting the specific friction from the agent side of a session that had already produced ten findings and twelve decisions. Written as FINDINGS-2026-08-12-agent-friction.md, matching the repository's existing dated-audit convention. Nine items of environmental friction, five of friction the agent caused, and one tension between two correct policies.

decisions.question: 'Friction from the agent side' — friction the agent experienced, or friction the agent caused?
decisions.commitment: Both, in two clearly separated sections. Section 1 is what the repository and container put in the agent's way, nine items, each ending with what would remove it. Section 2 is what the agent put in the operator's way, five items, four of them quoting the operator naming it first.
decisions.why: The phrase reads most naturally as the first, and the first alone would have been the more comfortable document to write — a list of things other people should fix. Three of the second section's items were raised by the operator out loud during the session, which means they were costing something visible while going unnoticed by the party causing them. Leaving that half out would have produced an accurate document that omitted the expensive half.

decisions.question: The document was requested after the fact rather than kept as the session ran. Does that limit it?
decisions.commitment: Yes, and it says so in its opening paragraph: it is reconstructed, so the small frictions are under-represented, because the ones routed around in ten seconds are the ones forgotten.
decisions.why: A friction log written from memory will over-weight the items that cost minutes and lose the ones that cost seconds, and the second class is usually larger and easier to fix. Stating the bias is cheap and stops a later reader treating the list as exhaustive — the same reason bench results carry their parameters rather than only their numbers.

decisions.question: Where does a friction record live — docs/ as a memo, or the root as a dated audit?
decisions.commitment: Root, as FINDINGS-2026-08-12-agent-friction.md, alongside the three existing FINDINGS files. The README already describes that family as 'dated audits, kept as records of what was found and how it was argued', and no test gates the file list there.
decisions.why: docs/ holds design memos addressed to whoever builds the thing next; this is addressed to whoever works here next, which is what the FINDINGS family is for. It also sidesteps test_docs.py's project-layout gate, which is a small practical win and not the reason — the convention fits on its own.

decisions.question: Section 2.4 records the same error twice in one session. Report both, or the general lesson once?
decisions.commitment: Both instances, named, with the general lesson stated after them rather than instead of them.
decisions.why: One instance reads as a slip and invites no change. Two ninety minutes apart, in different material, with the same shape — stop at the first plausible reading, assert the general case — is a description of how this agent fails, which is worth more to a later reader than either correction. Neither was caught by a gate; both were caught by looking again, and that is the only mechanism available.
